This bail cancellation application was filed on 20.05.2022.
The accused was granted bail by following order dated 20.04.2018 :-

"Heard Sri Kamlesh Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A.
for the State and perused the record.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No.624 of 2016, under Sections 376, 452, 323, 120B, 308 IPC and 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Karenda, District Ghaziabad, with the prayer to release him on bail.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the prosecutrix as per the medical report is aged about 18 years and from the tenor of her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., it appears that even prior to the incident the applicant had committed rape on her.
Learned counsel for the applicant states that prima facie, it appears that the prosecutrix is a major girl and she was a consenting party.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is in custody since 4.8.2016 having no criminal antecedent.
Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant but could not point out anything material to the contrary.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as also the submissions made,
without commenting upon merits of the case, I am of the opinion that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

Let applicant Pati Ram @ Raj Kumar, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions that :-
(1) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence; (2) The applicant shall not pressurize the prosecution witnesses; (3) The applicant shall appear on the date fixed by the trial Court.
In case of default of any of the conditions enumerated above, the Courts below shall be at liberty to cancel bail of the applicant. "
2. Accused is facing trial in a case arising out of Case Crime No.624 of 2016, under Sections 376,
452, 323, 120B, 308 IPC and 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Karenda, District Ghazipur.
3.

Sri Gyanendra Prasad Mahant, learned counsel for applicant refers paragraph Nos. 12, 13 and 14 that accused persons made a contact with victim and pressurized her so much that his marriage was broken.

Learned counsel fairly submits that during pendency of this application out of 9 proposed witnesses, 5 witnesses have already been examined and one witness has been discharged as such trial is at fag end.
He further submits that victim has made a statement before learned Trial Court which appears to be completely against accused.
4. Learned counsel for accused is not present.

5. In the aforesaid circumstances, considering that trial is proceeding and victim has fearlessly made her statement before Trial Court, as such in view of judgment passed by Supreme Court in Himanshu Sharma vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, 2024 SCC OnLine SC 187, I do not find any ground to allow this application, however, learned Trial court is directed to conclude the trial within period of six months from today and accused is directed to appear before concerned police station on every Nandini Kumari vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48730046/
2 Saturday to mark his presence along with undertaking that he will not make any contact with victim or her family members and in case of default, Trial Court is also at liberty to cancel bail of accused.
6.
